disposition_reason: Farm survey of 45 Trinidad and Tobago plantations reporting Cd ranges in cacao nibs and shells (testae) from unfermented, oven-dried beans, plus leaf, pod and soil Cd and Pearson correlations between tissues and soil. Only ranges are printed; no means, per-site or per-soil-type values.
disposition_locator: Section 4.1 (p. 40) for tissue ranges; Table 3 and Section 4.2 for correlations

study.material_scope: cacao bean nibs and shells (testae) from ripe pods, unfermented (rinsed of mucilage, oven-dried); leaves, pod husks and soils as context
study.growing_origin_vs_market: Grown in Trinidad and Tobago (45 plantations across soil types I-VII); field samples, not purchased
study.sampling_unit: plantation (8-12 randomly selected trees per site; leaves and ripe pods per tree, soil cores 0-30 cm at drip zone); whether reported ranges are per tree or per site is not stated
study.method: Concentrated HNO3 digestion (12 h pre-digest, 6 h at 130 °C), flame AAS
study.lod_loq: Cd: detection threshold stated only as 'detectable (>0.3 µg/g)'; no formal LOD/LOQ reported
study.basis: dry weight (beans rinsed of mucilage, oven-dried at 105 °C for 4-5 h, then separated into nibs and shells; Section 2.1)
study.qa: No cocoa CRM available; NIST SRM 1570a spinach leaves 2.69 ± 0.05 vs 2.89 µg/g certified (95.5% recovery); NIST SRM 2710 soil 99.0% recovery; 23 replicate CRM sets over an 18-month experimental period (Table 2)

findings.group: all sampled plantations, Trinidad and Tobago
findings.basis: dry weight (beans rinsed of mucilage, oven-dried at 105 °C for 4-5 h, then separated into nibs and shells; Section 2.1)
findings.censoring: Paper states only that 'more than 50% of the locations sampled contained detectable (>0.3 µg/g) Cd in the cacao tissues sampled'; the printed ranges therefore appear to cover quantified results only. Number of non-detect sites/trees per tissue not reported; not imputed.
findings.notes: Unfermented nibs (beans removed from ripe pods, rinsed, oven-dried, nibs separated from shells); concentrations are not for fermented/dried commercial beans. n per tissue not stated (45 plantations, 8-12 trees each). Ranges not broken down by site, cultivar or soil type.

findings.group: all sampled plantations, Trinidad and Tobago
findings.basis: dry weight (beans rinsed of mucilage, oven-dried at 105 °C for 4-5 h, then separated into nibs and shells; Section 2.1)
findings.censoring: Paper states only that 'more than 50% of the locations sampled contained detectable (>0.3 µg/g) Cd in the cacao tissues sampled'; the printed ranges therefore appear to cover quantified results only. Number of non-detect sites/trees per tissue not reported; not imputed.
findings.notes: Shells of unfermented, oven-dried beans. Shell > nib order reported (leaves > pods > shells > nibs).

controls.control: Pre-harvest screening of bean Cd from leaf or pod-husk Cd (tissue-to-tissue correlation)
controls.comparator: Pearson correlation of nib Cd with other tissues across sites
controls.outcome: nib/shell r = 0.86, nib/leaf r = 0.79, nib/pod r = 0.76, shell/leaf r = 0.83, shell/pod r = 0.68, leaf/pod r = 0.80 (all p < 0.05); authors propose estimating bean Cd from leaves/pods when pods are unavailable and monitoring soil treatments via tissue Cd. No validation of prediction error reported.

controls.control: Use bioavailable (DTPA/AB-DTPA/EDTA) rather than total HNO3-extractable soil Cd to assess farm risk
controls.comparator: total HNO3-extractable soil Cd (0.3-1.7 µg/g) vs tissue Cd
controls.outcome: nib/soil r = 0.35, shell/soil r = 0.43, leaf/soil r = 0.34, pod/soil r = 0.50 (significant but weak); authors conclude total soil Cd may not reflect plant availability

controls.control: Context: candidate Cd sources at higher-Cd sites (volcanic soils, flood-prone areas with possible industrial input, long history of phosphate fertilizer, recycling of leaf and pod litter)

contradictions_with_stored_summary: Stored summary 'Implications' says nib Cd up to 3.82 µg/g 'exceeds the EU maximum level for cocoa beans (0.30 mg/kg as of Regulation 488/2014 amendment period)'. The primary text cites only a 'proposed European Union standard' for beans and gives no 0.30 mg/kg value; Regulation 488/2014 sets limits for chocolate and cocoa powder products, not raw beans.
Stored summary says nib values are 'across soil types'; the paper prints only overall tissue ranges with no breakdown by soil type, site or cultivar.

Stored summary omits that beans were unfermented (rinsed, oven-dried at 105 °C), and that shells (0.44-4.41 µg/g) were measured; it also omits pod/soil and shell/soil correlations (0.50, 0.43 listed only partly).
Stored 'Trinidad and Tobago is a secondary high-Cd cacao origin ... with documented exceedances' is an interpretation not made in the paper.
unresolved: Collection dates not reported (only an '18-month experimental period' for CRM QC); years left null.
Number of nib and shell analyses (trees vs plantations) behind each range not stated; n left null.
Share of sites/tissues below the ~0.3 µg/g detection threshold not reported per tissue.
Cultivars sampled not named ('wide variety of cacao cultivars').
